Sam —

Thanks for the clarity — that helps. Looping in Ben (pricing lead) and Karthik (solutions/infra) so we can put concrete language around rollback windows and feature portability. I’ve attached three concise artifacts:
1) tier-chooser-matrix.xlsx — side-by-side scenarios and expected per-token economics
2) hot-swap-runbook.pdf — operational steps to toggle features with near-zero downtime (prefix/KV cache routing and canary routing patterns)
3) OptiHealth_MAProposal_v2.pdf — draft commercial with two recommended paths and indicative discount ranges

High-level summary (pick-a-path):
- Conservative upgrade (recommended for Execs focused on cost predictability): Start on Compact tier + reserved Burst pool for peak inference. Benefits: low upfront, easier rollback (30‑day rollback window available as a sanctioned downgrade with pro‑rata credit for unused months). Typical uplift: 10–14% list discount for 12‑month billing with a 6‑month pilot and usage thresholds.

- Hybrid burst (short-term pilot + headroom): Reserved throughput for core workloads, plus burst Dedicated capacity for spikes. Benefits: predictable baseline cost, lower risk to product org. Discounting: 12–16% depending on committed throughput.

- Throughput-first reserved (recommended if throughput SLA is the priority): Full reserved throughput (annual commit) with feature bundle that includes prioritized KV cache & extended retention. Benefits: lowest unit cost at scale; downgrade has a stepdown fee (standard stepdown ladder) unless agreement includes a rollback grace window. Discounting: 16–22% for larger annual deals.

Rollback & downgrade mechanics (short version):
- We can guarantee a 30‑day rollback window for an initial upgrade if opted into the Conservative upgrade path; rollback is effected by re-routing traffic and adjusting reservations — customer receives pro‑rata credits for unused reserved capacity.
- For full reserved annual purchases that include bundled add‑ons, rollbacks incur stepdown fees unless specifically carved out.

Pricing levers we recommend for OptiHealth pilot: commit to a 6‑month pilot with an annual option to convert; include a rollover credit for pilot unused capacity; use a canary route so product teams can trial features per-team without changing the global tier.

Next steps:
- If you want the Conservative upgrade, I’ll turn the matrix into an official quote with specific quantities and a proposed DocuSign.
- If you want the Hybrid path, Karthik can scope burst capacity ranges and expected latency SLOs in a short doc.

Can we lock a 30‑minute workshop this Friday 10–10:30am PST to finalize pilot quantities? I’ll bring the quote skeleton so Ben can annotate discount structure live.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
